section_1.title: Prerequisites & Definitions
section_1.content: Define a planar graph (can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing) and identify the three fundamental components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F).
section_1.example: Visualize a simple triangle graph: 3 vertices, 3 edges, and 2 faces (the inner triangle and the infinite exterior region).

section_2.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
section_2.content: Introduce the formula V - E + F = 2. Explain how this invariant constant holds for any connected planar graph regardless of its complexity.
section_2.example: Demonstrate with a square with one diagonal (4 vertices, 5 edges, 3 faces): 4 - 5 + 3 = 2. It holds perfectly!

section_3.title: The Concept of Dual Graphs
section_3.content: Explain the geometric transformation: place a node in each face of the original graph and connect nodes if their respective faces share an edge.
section_3.example: Imagine a honeybee hive (hexagonal grid). The dual graph turns every hexagonal cell into a vertex, creating a triangular lattice connecting the centers.

section_4.title: Duality Mechanics & Symmetry
section_4.content: Show the transformation rules: V_dual = F_original, F_dual = V_original, and E_dual = E_original. Explain that duality is a reciprocal relationship.
section_4.example: Transform a 3D-projected cube (8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 faces) into its dual: the Octahedron (6 vertices, 12 edges, 8 faces).

section_5.title: Application & Wrap-up
section_5.content: Connect duality to real-world circuit layout or network design, where shifting from nodes to regions helps solve complex routing problems.
section_5.example: Using dual graphs to optimize the pathing of a delivery robot navigating through distinct zones (faces) of a warehouse floor.

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Characteristic Formula", [
            "Euler's formula states V minus E plus F equals 2.",
            "This constant invariant holds for connected planar graphs.",
            "A square with a diagonal validates the formula."
        ])

            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[0].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color="#00FF00")
        ]
        graph = VGroup(*nodes, *edges)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        calc = MathTex(r"4 - 5 + 3 = 2", color="#FFFFFF")

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
